title: What If You Watched a Sunset on Mars? It Turns Blue

scenes.text: What if you watched the Sun set on Mars? The sky does the opposite of Earth.
Mars is 141.6 million miles from the Sun, so it looks smaller, about 0.35 degrees wide instead of 0.5.
By day, dust absorbs blue light and the sky away from the Sun looks reddish.
As the Sun sinks, fine dust scatters blue light forward and a cool blue glow forms around it.
NASA's Curiosity rover caught it on April 15, 2015, in a sequence lasting 6 minutes 51 seconds.
Then twilight lingers for two hours or more, because lofted dust stays lit high above you. On Mars, sunsets are blue and the night is slow.

description:
What if you watched the Sun set on Mars?
